hero.title: Understand your medical bills
hero.lead: Medical bills, subsidies and medicine labels, explained in plain words and read aloud. Made for Ah Ma, Ah Gong and the family who care for them.

scan.title: Snap a photo. We explain it simply.
scan.text: Point your phone at a bill or a medicine label. We tell you what each line means, what is already paid for, and what you still need to pay.

listen.title: Hear it in your own language.
listen.text: Pick a language, then tap the big button. We read everything out slowly and clearly, as many times as you need.
listen.hint: Tap the big button to listen
listen.hintSpeaking: Reading aloud now. Tap again to stop.

doses.title: Morning, afternoon, night. All sorted.
doses.text: We turn your medicine labels into a simple daily plan, and remind you when it is time.

ask.title: No question is too small.
ask.text: Type or speak your question and get a short, kind answer in simple words, any time of the day.
ask.q1: Can I take my blood pressure pill with kopi?
ask.a1: Yes, kopi is fine with your blood pressure pill. Take it after breakfast, same as always.
ask.q2: Thank you! Can you read that out for Ah Gong?
ask.a2: Of course. Tap Read aloud under my answer, and Ah Gong can hear it.
ask.q3: How should I keep my medicines?
ask.a3: Keep them in a cool, dry place, away from sunlight and out of reach of children.
ask.q4: Can I stop my pills when I feel better?
ask.a4: Please don't stop on your own. Ask your doctor or pharmacist first.

landing.note: Ah Ma Ah Gong Can helps you understand. Your doctor and pharmacist still make the decisions.

bill.lead: Tap any line to see what it means.
bill.scope: Works with medical bills from Singapore clinics, hospitals, dental clinics and pharmacies. Subsidy estimates are for polyclinic, GP and dental bills only.

explain.consultation: This is the fee for seeing the doctor or nurse at the clinic.
explain.medication: These are the medicines you were given to take home. The price depends on the medicine and how much you got.
explain.investigation: These are tests that help the doctor check your health, such as blood tests, urine tests or X-rays.
explain.procedure: This is treatment done during your visit, such as cleaning and dressing a wound, or an injection.
explain.ward: This is the charge for your hospital bed and room, usually for each day you stayed.
explain.tax: GST (Goods and Services Tax) is a tax added to the bill. It is not a medical charge.
explain.other: This is another charge, such as dressing materials or a medical memo. Ask at the counter if you are not sure what it is.

scheme.government: The government pays part of the cost of your care. This amount has already been taken off your bill.
scheme.chas: CHAS (Community Health Assist Scheme) is a government scheme that helps Singaporeans pay for clinic visits. This amount has already been taken off your bill.
scheme.pioneer: The Pioneer Generation gets extra help with healthcare costs. If you are in it, you have a Pioneer Generation card. This amount has already been taken off your bill.
scheme.merdeka: The Merdeka Generation gets extra help with healthcare costs. If you are in it, you have a Merdeka Generation card. This amount has already been taken off your bill.
scheme.insurance: MediShield Life or your insurance plan paid this part of the bill. You don’t pay this amount.
scheme.other: Another scheme or discount took this amount off your bill. Ask at the counter which one it is.

explain.medisave: MediSave is your CPF savings for healthcare. Money from it can pay part of some bills, so you pay less in cash.
explain.medisaveNone: Nothing was paid from MediSave on this bill.

rules.pioneer: For Singapore citizens born in 1949 or earlier who became citizens by 1986. At polyclinics, you get an extra 50% off the rest of your bill for subsidised services and medicines. You also get extra help at CHAS GP clinics.
rules.merdeka: For Singapore citizens born from 1950 to 1959 who became citizens by 1996, and older citizens who did not get the Pioneer Generation Package. At polyclinics, you get an extra 25% off the rest of your bill for subsidised services and medicines. You also get extra help at CHAS GP clinics.
rules.chas: All Singapore citizens can apply for CHAS. It gives subsidies at CHAS GP and dental clinics only, not at polyclinics. Your card colour (Blue, Orange or Green) depends on your household’s monthly income per person.
rules.polyclinic: Singapore citizens and permanent residents pay subsidised rates at polyclinics. The subsidy is already taken off your polyclinic bill.
